source.title: PIPELINE GATE 05/09 — Verified Supplier Offer Fast Lane & Atomic Commit
source.body:
# PIPELINE GATE 05/09 — Known SKU Supplier Offer Fast Lane & Safe Commit

**Purpose:** after approved Stage 03 semantics and verified Stage 04 exact SKU identity, update *supplier-specific* price/availability signals with minimal latency and **zero AI calls** for known SKUs. This checkpoint audits/reuses existing AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#136 (SG-05), AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#135 (SG-04), AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#93 supplier PO workflow; it does **not** rebuild the Sourcing module. Parent AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#144; stage is NOT verified/implemented by this issue alone.

## Happy path

(1) Receive Stage 04 verified supplierId + canonicalSkuId and approved source profile/version, source kind, import mode (partial/full), row and field presence with raw evidence. (2) Fetch current SupplierOffer values in a batch. (3) Compute typed BEFORE→AFTER diff and unit economics **after aligning piece/carton/pack/bonus quantity and discount basis**. (4) Apply eligible changes atomically with source/provenance/audit, freshness/revision checks, idempotency and scoped permissions. (5) Report updated/unchanged/held/skipped/failed per row; leave unmatched/new Candidates to separate Stage 06 path. No AI blocking.

## Tested design precedents / avoid reinvention

* PostgreSQL 17 `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE` supports conditional atomic conflict updates; use supplier+SKU uniqueness (or equivalent existing key) and freshness/revision compare rather than unconditional last-write-wins. Official: [https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-insert.html](<https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-insert.html>)
* Existing Prisma version and transaction API must be inspected before coding. If compatible, scoped transactions with appropriate isolation/retries (e.g. P2034 on supported versions) avoid concurrent anomalies. Official v6: [https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/v6/prisma-client/queries/transactions](<https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/v6/prisma-client/queries/transactions>) ; current docs APIs can differ.
* Salesforce Commerce inventory IMPEX guidance distinguishes delta updates from full imports, recommends not clearing absent records and handles idempotent event records/effective dates. Conceptual source only, **do not install Salesforce**: [https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/sfra/guide/inventory-impex-best-practices.html](<https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/sfra/guide/inventory-impex-best-practices.html>)
* Stripe's API idempotency describes a useful established retry pattern with a unique key+payload identity; conceptual reference only, **do not install Stripe or payment SDK**: [https://stripe.com/blog/idempotency](<https://stripe.com/blog/idempotency>)

## Required invariants

* **SupplierOffer, not Product/SKU identity or public SellingPrice, is mutated.** Supplier reported quantity is a signal, not reservation/Hub stock/customer sellability guarantee.
* **PARTIAL_UPDATE** applies ONLY explicitly supplied fields. Blank/missing is not zero; verified zero quantity may set availability to zero only under supported source semantics.
* **FULL_SNAPSHOT** may deactivate omitted supplier offers ONLY when authoritatively complete for exactly an approved supplier/catalog/field scope, with measured anomaly checks + explicit authorization. A random supplier price list or cropped file is not full inventory truth. Safest MVP default: absence never deactivates.
* Approved older/awarded/received POs retain their committed cost/qty snapshot and supplier history; new offer update cannot retrospectively rewrite procurement commitments or customer's accepted quote.
* Price-only file does not overwrite availability; stock-only file does not overwrite cost; supplier MSRP/reference retail != confirmed purchase cost.
* No unverified sell-at-loss. Cost comparisons only for same verified sellable unit and actual *approved* ShinaCare sale price, with known direct-cost basis; uncertain economics → HOLD/ALERT, not forged margin or automatic retail repricing.
* Exactly-once logical commit per batch+approved profile/revision/row or proven idempotent outcome; retry/concurrency cannot duplicate changes or delete inventory.
* Source observedAt/effectiveAt, approved profile revision, source fields and stale/out-of-order commit guard; never blindly overwrite newer known prices/stock from an older file.
* Scoped supplier authorization, audit provenance, money as exact decimal (no floating-point rounding of EGP/discount), no sensitive other-supplier commercial pricing leakage.

## Adversarial scenarios → expected outcome

 1. Known SKU 500-qty/price update with no changed fields → UNCHANGED, no duplicate writes.
 2. Only price present and quantity absent vs explicit 0 qty → field-specific update vs qualified zero; preserve missing.
 3. 500 EGP for carton of 5 vs approved retail 300 EGP per individual item → compare 100/item, no spurious loss block; 500/item vs sell 300/item → FINANCIAL_HOLD for procurement/sellability review, don't overwrite customer sale price.
 4. Retail reference only vs supplier purchase cost unknown → hold cost update; do not fabricate purchase price.
 5. Supplier says batch FULL but only 20% of agreed product coverage; mass vanish/price spikes → HOLD snapshot deactivation; no silent disable.
 6. Old invoice, out-of-order timestamp, retry same content, double Apply button and concurrent supplier imports → conflict/replay-safe; preserve latest accepted state with trace.
 7. Duplicate same SKU rows with differing prices/qty in one batch → REVIEW/reconciliation; no arbitrarily select last row.
 8. Same canonical SKU from supplier A and B → each supplier offer separate; supplier A cannot access or rewrite supplier B.
 9. AI enrichment offline or NEW candidates pending → known supplier offer updates still succeed independently.
10. Accepted PO quantity/cost, quote and Hub receiving in flight during supplier update → snapshots immutable and no retroactive financial/custody mismatch.
11. DB timeout at chunk boundary, crash after commit but before response → idempotent replay + persisted row outcomes / resumable errors; partial failure visible, no false all-success.
12. Unsafe discounts, negative price, impossible percent, pack/bonus basis confusion, currency not EGP, abnormal price delta → row REVIEW/INVALID with reason and no dangerous offer change.

## Implementation technique / security

Audit existing NestJS+Prisma ingestion/offer-batch commit service and supplier authorization. Reuse reviewed alias fast path and existing supplier offers. Consider one batched lookup, staged diffs, bounded transaction chunks, existing uniqueness and audit structures; only add SQL conditional UPSERT or schema constraints where an actual proven gap requires it. No new queue, event bus, microservice, Elasticsearch or AI architecture by default. A huge transaction is not mandatory for unrelated rows, but full snapshot deactivation must never leave inconsistent partial applied coverage. Test writes/adversarial cases on isolated local \_test PostgreSQL ONLY; preserve real Supabase and unrelated commits.

## Required acceptance (all evidenced before PASS)

- [ ] Real repo SHA/schema/Prisma version/current Stage 05 code and source paths audited.
- [ ] Known 1000-row supplier file updates verified products/offers with **zero AI calls**; measured query count, throughput and p50/p95 (do not invent numbers).
- [ ] Partial/full/unknown/zero, cost-vs-retail, pack/bonus/unit tests pass in \_test DB with before/after evidence.
- [ ] Older batches, content replay, double-commit, concurrency and modified mappings do not corrupt last accepted data.
- [ ] All cross-supplier isolation and role permission negative cases pass.
- [ ] Accepted POs/customer pricing/Hub stock remain unchanged and truthful.
- [ ] One row fails while safe independent rows proceed as explicit partial outcomes; all rows accounted, statuses reflected in supplier UI.
- [ ] Commit rollback/restart and crash-after-commit replays produce no fake success or lost committed results.
- [ ] Report exact tests, known blockers, risk decision and GO/NO-GO.

**Hard STOP:** mass offer deactivation without proven full scope; stale update overwrites fresh data; cross-tenant commit; old PO mutation; public selling-price overwrite; double debit/commit; unsafe financial data applied as valid.

**Stage 06 next:** NEW_CANDIDATE and reusable Brand/Line/Ingredient research workflow; this must not block known SKU fast lane.

## Owner addendum — File Age Validation, Source Freshness & Supplier Staleness Alerts (22 Oct 2026)

**Owner-requested; FUTURE implementation requirement of Stage 05, not an automated reminder set by ChatGPT.**

1. On intake retain separately: server upload receivedAt (trusted time of receipt), original workbook properties created/modified (untrusted advisory metadata), source-reported export/generatedAt or effectiveAt if present (supplier-reported, not cryptographically verified), and last SUCCESSFULLY ACCEPTED supplier offer update at. Do not equate any two dates. CSV often has no internal createdAt; copied/exported XLSX can carry stale/changed metadata.
2. Date sanity checks: missing/unparseable/absurd future/older-than-latest accepted, unexpected export cadence, source time zone/date-only ambiguity and identical file hash with newer upload time. Do not allow a re-upload with a fresh upload timestamp to overwrite newer offer truth or reset freshness. File created date alone is insufficient to assume stock accuracy or to hard-block a valid update; apply priority to source semantics + observedAt + accepted version, and HOLD suspicious conflicting updates for review.
3. Per-supplier **owner-configured refresh cadence** and grace period, independent of PO-response SLA. Track last meaningful successfully validated refresh (and separately last attempted upload); stale source when threshold elapsed. Never invent default '12 hours' as supplier-file freshness policy without explicit business config.
4. Notification design: supplier workspace first, then approved notification channel (e.g. WhatsApp fallback only if actually configured/consented); include current last accepted timestamp, freshness age, next upload action and missing/error cause, **one alert per stale episode with rate limit**. Internal operations escalate only when stale inventory/sourcing affects sellability, purchases or commitments. Suppress repeat alerts on active issue, reset only after genuine verified newer data, not uploaded junk/dedup file.
5. Supplier disabled/on leave/pilot paused/after hours or no obligation to refresh → pause configured alert rather than spam. Identity, documentKind and offer-specific cost vs quantity freshness separately tracked; a price-only refresh must not mark stock fresh.
6. **Adversarial acceptance:** stale workbook metadata but actually current verified export, forged fresh metadata on stale content, future dates/timezone, same file uploaded twice, 2-day-old file uploaded today, price-only when stock stale, last upload rejected, no offer rows accepted, multiple reminders dedup, cross-supplier notification isolation. Require real fixtures + DB before/after + UI notification evidence before PASS.
7. Use existing NestJS service, Prisma persisted audit/source fields and existing notification mechanism if present. No new scheduler/provider unless demonstrated necessary; ordinary scheduled DB query adequate for MVP. Do not overclaim actual product availability from any file timestamp.

## Stage 08 pricing boundary (22 Oct 2026)

Do not pick supplier for future PO just because supplier offer updated; Storefront SellingPrice and existing approved PO cost remain separate. When sourcing/approval needs to compare suppliers, consume current approved SupplierOffer data using the EXISTING Sourcing/PO engine under Stage 08 AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#166, normalized to same SKU/unit and confirmed feasibility. Mean/median across vendors is anomaly-signal not an operational cost/retail price. Avoid creating a second supplier ranking algorithm in ingestion.
